title: Evaluation of two treatment protocols in supportive periodontal therapy: effectiveness, efficiency and patient comfort in context of student-delivered treatments
summary: This study compares two methods of professional teeth cleaning in patients undergoing supportive periodontitis therapy (UPT). One group will be treated using an air-polishing method (Guided Biofilm Therapy, GBT), while the other will receive a cleaning with ultrasonic instruments and polishing paste. The goal is to determine whether dental students achieve equally good results with the GBT method in terms of cleaning effectiveness, treatment duration, and patient comfort.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients with a diagnosis of periodontitis therapy (UPT), ≥ 10 natural teeth, signed declaration of consent
Exclusion criteria:
Patients with a diagnosis of periodontitis with ongoing pre-treatment or anti-infective therapy (root planing), lack of knowledge of the German language, dental students or dental professionals, ≥ 50 revitalised teeth, infectious diseases (HIV, hepatitis C, etc.), Contraindication for ultrasonic devices: Pacemaers, contraindication for air-polishing devices: respiratory diseases (asthma, COPD, tubercolusis, etc.), allergies (CHX, erythritol)
